stem: A bedbound patient has intact but nonblanchable redness over the coccyx. Which care-plan change is most appropriate?
option_a: Use vigorous massage each shift
option_b: Place a ring-shaped cushion under the area
option_c: Wait for an open wound before changing care
option_d: Offload the area, manage moisture and increase focused skin reassessment

option_rationales.a: Massage can further injure vulnerable tissue.
option_rationales.b: Ring cushions concentrate surrounding pressure.
option_rationales.d: Early pressure injury needs sustained pressure relief and monitoring.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Massage can further injure vulnerable tissue. B: Ring cushions concentrate surrounding pressure. C: Prevention must begin before breakdown. D: Early pressure injury needs sustained pressure relief and monitoring.

stem: A patient recovering from a stroke begins coughing after sips of thin liquid. What should the RN do?
option_a: Stop oral intake, assess the airway and arrange a swallowing reassessment
option_b: Give a straw to help coordinate the swallow
option_c: Offer larger sips to clear secretions
option_d: Continue liquids and document the cough as normal

option_rationales.a: Coughing with liquids raises concern for aspiration.
option_rationales.b: A straw may worsen aspiration in some patients.
option_rationales.d: Continuing without evaluation is unsafe.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Coughing with liquids raises concern for aspiration. B: A straw may worsen aspiration in some patients. C: Larger volumes may increase risk. D: Continuing without evaluation is unsafe.

stem: A patient receiving oxygen through a nasal cannula reports dry mouth and has trouble brushing teeth independently. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Restrict oral care to once weekly
option_b: Provide regular assisted oral care and approved moisturization
option_c: Apply unapproved oil-based products inside the nose
option_d: Stop oxygen without checking the order

option_rationales.a: Infrequent care worsens discomfort and oral infection risk.
option_rationales.b: Assisted hygiene helps comfort and mucosal integrity.
option_rationales.c: Oil-based products may raise oxygen-related safety concerns.
option_rationales.d: Stopping oxygen can cause hypoxemia.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Infrequent care worsens discomfort and oral infection risk. B: Assisted hygiene helps comfort and mucosal integrity. C: Oil-based products may raise oxygen-related safety concerns. D: Stopping oxygen can cause hypoxemia.

stem: A stable patient with a new colostomy fears changing the pouch at home. Which nursing approach is best?
option_a: Change every pouch without allowing participation
option_b: Tell the patient it is too difficult to learn
option_c: Demonstrate one step at a time and support supervised return-demonstration
option_d: Send written instructions without practice

option_rationales.a: Excluding the patient reduces confidence.
option_rationales.b: Discouragement undermines self-care.
option_rationales.d: Written material alone may not establish skill.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Excluding the patient reduces confidence. B: Discouragement undermines self-care. C: Graduated practice helps develop competence. D: Written material alone may not establish skill.

stem: A patient on opioids reports hard stools despite an ordered stool-softening regimen. Which additional assessment is most helpful?
option_a: Favorite television programs
option_b: Usual footwear
option_c: Date of last dental cleaning
option_d: Fluid intake, activity, bowel pattern and current bowel medications

option_rationales.a: Entertainment does not explain constipation.
option_rationales.b: Footwear is not the first bowel assessment.
option_rationales.d: Contributing factors and treatment response guide bowel-plan adjustments.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Entertainment does not explain constipation. B: Footwear is not the first bowel assessment. C: Dental history is less relevant. D: Contributing factors and treatment response guide bowel-plan adjustments.

stem: A stable patient says repeated overnight vital-sign checks prevent sleep. Which response is most appropriate?
option_a: Review which monitoring is necessary and coordinate nonurgent care to protect sleep
option_b: Cancel all ordered monitoring without review
option_c: Tell the patient sleep is not part of nursing care
option_d: Offer unprescribed sleeping medication

option_rationales.a: Balancing necessary observations with clustered care supports sleep.
option_rationales.b: Unilateral cancellation may miss deterioration.
option_rationales.d: Unordered sedatives add risk.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Balancing necessary observations with clustered care supports sleep. B: Unilateral cancellation may miss deterioration. C: Sleep affects recovery. D: Unordered sedatives add risk.

stem: A parent reports a child missed a routine vaccine dose three months ago. What should the RN explain?
option_a: Every vaccine series must begin again
option_b: The immunization record can be reviewed against a catch-up schedule; valid doses usually count
option_c: No further immunization is possible
option_d: Give live vaccines during significant immunosuppression without review

option_rationales.a: Most vaccine series do not need restarting after a delay.
option_rationales.b: Catch-up guidance uses documented prior doses and intervals.
option_rationales.c: Delayed schedules can generally be resumed.
option_rationales.d: Immune status and contraindications matter.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Most vaccine series do not need restarting after a delay. B: Catch-up guidance uses documented prior doses and intervals. C: Delayed schedules can generally be resumed. D: Immune status and contraindications matter.

stem: A pregnant patient asks about avoiding foodborne illness. Which advice is appropriate?
option_a: Eat raw sprouts daily
option_b: Drink unpasteurized milk for additional nutrients
option_c: Avoid unpasteurized dairy products and heat higher-risk deli meats as recommended
option_d: Rely on odor to identify all harmful bacteria

option_rationales.a: Raw sprouts may harbor pathogens.
option_rationales.b: Unpasteurized dairy increases listeriosis risk.
option_rationales.c: Pregnancy increases consequences of some foodborne infections.
option_rationales.d: Contaminated food may smell normal.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Raw sprouts may harbor pathogens. B: Unpasteurized dairy increases listeriosis risk. C: Pregnancy increases consequences of some foodborne infections. D: Contaminated food may smell normal.

stem: A patient with diabetes and influenza asks whether to stop all glucose checks because appetite is poor. What should the nurse say?
option_a: Monitoring is only needed on workdays
option_b: Avoid drinking fluids while feverish
option_c: Double all diabetes medications automatically
option_d: Continue glucose monitoring as directed and contact the care team for individualized sick-day medication instructions

option_rationales.a: Illness can change glucose even without usual eating.
option_rationales.b: Dehydration can worsen illness.
option_rationales.d: Sick-day plans include monitoring, hydration and medication guidance.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Illness can change glucose even without usual eating. B: Dehydration can worsen illness. C: Automatic doubling risks hypoglycemia. D: Sick-day plans include monitoring, hydration and medication guidance.

stem: Which patient statement demonstrates understanding of home blood-pressure monitoring?
option_a: 'I'll sit quietly, support my arm at heart level and record readings for review.'
option_b: 'I'll measure immediately after drinking coffee and climbing stairs.'
option_c: 'I'll adjust my medication based on one high reading.'
option_d: 'I'll use my wrist cuff loosely over a jacket sleeve.'

option_rationales.a: Consistent technique and logs support accurate interpretation.
option_rationales.b: Caffeine and exertion can distort readings.
option_rationales.c: Medication changes require an individualized plan.
option_rationales.d: Loose clothing-interfered measurements are unreliable.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Consistent technique and logs support accurate interpretation. B: Caffeine and exertion can distort readings. C: Medication changes require an individualized plan. D: Loose clothing-interfered measurements are unreliable.

stem: A patient trying to quit smoking says they smoked one cigarette after two weeks tobacco-free. What is the best RN response?
option_a: Tell them the quit attempt has failed
option_b: Discuss the trigger and help plan how to respond to a similar situation next time
option_c: Suggest smoking only after meals
option_d: Avoid discussing the lapse

option_rationales.a: A lapse need not equal relapse.
option_rationales.b: Problem-solving and support promote continued cessation.
option_rationales.d: Avoidance misses a teachable opportunity.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: A lapse need not equal relapse. B: Problem-solving and support promote continued cessation. C: Scheduled smoking maintains dependence. D: Avoidance misses a teachable opportunity.

stem: A patient whose spouse died recently says, 'Everyone tells me to move on, but I can't.' What should the nurse say?
option_a: 'You should try to stop thinking about it.'
option_b: 'Time heals everything in exactly six weeks.'
option_c: 'It sounds painful to feel pressured. Tell me what the days have been like.'
option_d: 'Let's discuss something cheerful instead.'

option_rationales.a: Suppression is not supportive.
option_rationales.b: Grief has no fixed timetable.
option_rationales.c: Reflection and open questions validate the experience.
option_rationales.d: Changing the subject can shut down disclosure.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Suppression is not supportive. B: Grief has no fixed timetable. C: Reflection and open questions validate the experience. D: Changing the subject can shut down disclosure.

stem: A patient newly diagnosed with schizophrenia says, 'My neighbors put a camera in my teeth.' What is the most therapeutic response?
option_a: 'Yes, the cameras are real.'
option_b: 'That's ridiculous; stop saying it.'
option_c: 'Tell your neighbors to remove it.'
option_d: 'I don't have evidence of a camera, but I can see this worries you. How can I help you feel safe?'

option_rationales.a: Agreeing reinforces the delusion.
option_rationales.b: Confrontational dismissal harms rapport.
option_rationales.d: Acknowledging emotion without affirming the belief supports therapeutic communication.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Agreeing reinforces the delusion. B: Confrontational dismissal harms rapport. C: Encouraging confrontation may increase danger. D: Acknowledging emotion without affirming the belief supports therapeutic communication.

stem: A patient says, 'I have been saving my pills because I don't want to be here anymore.' What is the priority?
option_a: Assess imminent risk, secure access to medications and activate appropriate safety response
option_b: Promise secrecy to build trust
option_c: Leave the patient alone to rest
option_d: Recommend a routine appointment in three months

option_rationales.a: Access to means and expressed intent require immediate safeguards.
option_rationales.b: Safety concerns cannot be kept confidential when protection is needed.
option_rationales.d: Deferral may miss acute risk.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Access to means and expressed intent require immediate safeguards. B: Safety concerns cannot be kept confidential when protection is needed. C: Unsupervised access may increase danger. D: Deferral may miss acute risk.

stem: A patient becomes tense when staff begin an intimate examination without explaining each step. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Continue rapidly to finish before the patient protests
option_b: Pause, explain the steps, seek permission and offer appropriate choices
option_c: Tell the patient to tolerate the exam without questions
option_d: Ask additional observers into the room without consent

option_rationales.a: Proceeding without explanation may heighten trauma responses.
option_rationales.b: Permission and transparency preserve dignity and control.
option_rationales.d: Unnecessary observers may worsen distress.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Proceeding without explanation may heighten trauma responses. B: Permission and transparency preserve dignity and control. C: Coercion undermines therapeutic care. D: Unnecessary observers may worsen distress.

stem: A patient with asthma is initially wheezing loudly. Later they become drowsy and breath sounds are barely audible despite marked work of breathing. What does this indicate?
option_a: The attack has resolved
option_b: The patient simply needs sleep
option_c: Potential impending respiratory failure requiring emergency help
option_d: A normal effect of inhaled medication

option_rationales.a: Quiet breath sounds may indicate critically reduced airflow.
option_rationales.b: Drowsiness during distress is a danger sign.
option_rationales.c: Fatigue and a silent chest signal severe deterioration.
option_rationales.d: This is not a reassuring treatment effect.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Quiet breath sounds may indicate critically reduced airflow. B: Drowsiness during distress is a danger sign. C: Fatigue and a silent chest signal severe deterioration. D: This is not a reassuring treatment effect.

stem: A patient with kidney disease has potassium 6.8 mEq/L and widening QRS complexes. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
option_a: Encourage a potassium-rich snack
option_b: Wait for the next routine lab draw
option_c: Administer oral potassium supplement
option_d: Activate urgent response, monitor rhythm and prepare prescribed emergency treatment

option_rationales.a: Additional potassium worsens the problem.
option_rationales.b: ECG changes make this time-sensitive.
option_rationales.d: Hyperkalemia with conduction changes can precipitate arrest.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Additional potassium worsens the problem. B: ECG changes make this time-sensitive. C: Potassium supplementation is contraindicated. D: Hyperkalemia with conduction changes can precipitate arrest.

stem: A patient with diabetes is unresponsive; glucose is 34 mg/dL. Which intervention should the nurse prepare?
option_a: Nonoral emergency glucose treatment per protocol while supporting airway and reassessing
option_b: A cup of juice by mouth
option_c: The next scheduled rapid-acting insulin dose
option_d: A brisk walk after waking

option_rationales.a: Unresponsiveness requires airway support and IV dextrose or glucagon according to access and orders.
option_rationales.b: Oral fluids risk aspiration.
option_rationales.d: Exercise is unsafe and irrelevant.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Unresponsiveness requires airway support and IV dextrose or glucagon according to access and orders. B: Oral fluids risk aspiration. C: Insulin worsens hypoglycemia. D: Exercise is unsafe and irrelevant.

stem: A patient with heart failure receives prescribed diuretics. Which change most suggests improved congestion?
option_a: New crackles and lower oxygen saturation
option_b: Reduced orthopnea, improved breathing and declining edema
option_c: Rapid weight gain and increasing ankle swelling
option_d: New pink frothy sputum

option_rationales.a: Worsening sounds and hypoxemia indicate deterioration.
option_rationales.b: Less congestion and easier breathing indicate treatment response.
option_rationales.d: Frothy sputum may signal pulmonary edema.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Worsening sounds and hypoxemia indicate deterioration. B: Less congestion and easier breathing indicate treatment response. C: Weight gain suggests retained fluid. D: Frothy sputum may signal pulmonary edema.

stem: A patient with atrial fibrillation suddenly cannot understand spoken instructions and has a right facial droop. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Offer water to assess swallowing
option_b: Wait for symptoms to resolve
option_c: Activate the stroke response and record time last known well
option_d: Ask the patient to walk for observation

option_rationales.a: Possible dysphagia makes oral fluid unsafe.
option_rationales.b: Delay may lose time-sensitive treatment options.
option_rationales.c: New deficits warrant immediate stroke evaluation.
option_rationales.d: Walking may cause falls and delays care.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Possible dysphagia makes oral fluid unsafe. B: Delay may lose time-sensitive treatment options. C: New deficits warrant immediate stroke evaluation. D: Walking may cause falls and delays care.

stem: A patient being treated for pneumonia becomes newly confused with BP 82/44 mm Hg and urine output 10 mL/hr. What is the priority?
option_a: Provide routine education about pneumonia
option_b: Ask for a bedtime snack
option_c: Wait for morning laboratory tests
option_d: Escalate suspected shock and begin prescribed stabilization measures

option_rationales.a: Education follows stabilization.
option_rationales.b: Food does not address hypoperfusion.
option_rationales.d: Hypotension, oliguria and altered mentation suggest impaired perfusion.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Education follows stabilization. B: Food does not address hypoperfusion. C: Delay could worsen organ injury. D: Hypotension, oliguria and altered mentation suggest impaired perfusion.

stem: A toddler with vomiting has lethargy, delayed capillary refill and weak peripheral pulses. Which action is most appropriate?
option_a: Urgently assess for shock and prepare ordered isotonic resuscitation
option_b: Offer a large meal
option_c: Wait until the next diaper change before responding
option_d: Give an antidiarrheal without assessment

option_rationales.a: Poor perfusion with lethargy warrants rapid intervention.
option_rationales.b: Feeding is not first during shock.
option_rationales.d: Antidiarrheals do not correct shock.

rationale: Correct answer: A. A: Poor perfusion with lethargy warrants rapid intervention. B: Feeding is not first during shock. C: Deferral risks deterioration. D: Antidiarrheals do not correct shock.

stem: After bowel surgery, a patient develops increasing distention and vomiting without passing flatus. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Give a stimulant laxative immediately
option_b: Hold oral intake as indicated, assess fluid status and notify the clinician of possible ileus
option_c: Provide a large high-fiber meal
option_d: Encourage drinking carbonated beverages rapidly

option_rationales.a: Laxatives may be inappropriate in obstruction or ileus.
option_rationales.b: Symptoms require assessment and possible bowel rest.
option_rationales.d: Large fluids may worsen distention.

rationale: Correct answer: B. A: Laxatives may be inappropriate in obstruction or ileus. B: Symptoms require assessment and possible bowel rest. C: Solid food may aggravate vomiting. D: Large fluids may worsen distention.

stem: Ten minutes after starting red-cell transfusion, a patient develops chills, fever and back pain. Which action is priority?
option_a: Slow the rate and continue monitoring
option_b: Give the next unit first
option_c: Stop transfusion immediately and follow reaction protocol while assessing the patient
option_d: Have the patient stand to improve circulation

option_rationales.a: Continued exposure may worsen a severe reaction.
option_rationales.b: More blood may be dangerous.
option_rationales.c: Suspected acute reaction requires immediate cessation and support.
option_rationales.d: Standing is unsafe during a possible reaction.

rationale: Correct answer: C. A: Continued exposure may worsen a severe reaction. B: More blood may be dangerous. C: Suspected acute reaction requires immediate cessation and support. D: Standing is unsafe during a possible reaction.

stem: On postoperative day three, a patient reports sudden pleuritic chest pain, rapid respirations and oxygen saturation 86%. What should the nurse do?
option_a: Offer an oral pain pill and reassess in an hour
option_b: Ask the patient to ambulate
option_c: Schedule routine imaging for tomorrow
option_d: Support airway and oxygenation and summon urgent evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism

option_rationales.a: Pain management alone delays evaluation.
option_rationales.b: Ambulation is unsafe during acute cardiopulmonary compromise.
option_rationales.c: Imaging may be needed but should not delay stabilization.
option_rationales.d: Sudden hypoxemia and pleuritic pain suggest an acute emergency.

rationale: Correct answer: D. A: Pain management alone delays evaluation. B: Ambulation is unsafe during acute cardiopulmonary compromise. C: Imaging may be needed but should not delay stabilization. D: Sudden hypoxemia and pleuritic pain suggest an acute emergency.
